title: Validating the skellam package
text: definition, \(P(X = x) = \sum_k P(Y_1 = k + x)\,P(Y_2 = k)\). Summing series directly slow exact, makes good reference. probabilities also add one, including rates far beyond series can handle quickly: one rate zero distribution Poisson, Poisson turned upside :
code: pmf_by_sum <- function(x, l1, l2) {   k <- max(0, -x):(abs(x) + 200 + 20 * (l1 + l2))   sum(dpois(k + x, l1) * dpois(k, l2)) } x <- -10:15 for (L in list(c(1.5, 0.5), c(12, 8))) {   ref <- vapply(x, pmf_by_sum, 0, l1 = L[1], l2 = L[2])   cat(sprintf("lambda = (%g, %g): largest relative difference %.1e\n",               L[1], L[2], max(abs(dskellam(x, L[1], L[2]) / ref - 1)))) } #> lambda = (1.5, 0.5): largest relative difference 6.7e-15 #> lambda = (12, 8): largest relative difference 2.7e-15 for (L in list(c(1.5, 0.5), c(12, 8), c(1e4, 1e4), c(1e6, 1e6))) {   s <- sqrt(sum(L)); m <- L[1] - L[2]   x <- seq(floor(m - 30 * s), ceiling(m + 30 * s))   cat(sprintf("lambda = (%g, %g): 1 - sum = %.1e\n", L[1], L[2],               1 - sum(dskellam(x, L[1], L[2])))) } #> lambda = (1.5, 0.5): 1 - sum = 0.0e+00 #> lambda = (12, 8): 1 - sum = -8.9e-16 #> lambda = (10000, 10000): 1 - sum = 0.0e+00 #> lambda = (1e+06, 1e+06): 1 - sum = 0.0e+00 all.equal(dskellam(0:10, 5, 0), dpois(0:10, 5)) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(dskellam(-(0:10), 0, 5), dpois(0:10, 5)) #> [1] TRUE

title: The Skellam Distribution — skellam
text: \(Y_1 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_1)\) \(Y_2 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_2)\) independent, \(X = Y_1 - Y_2\) Skellam distribution probability mass function $$P(X = x) = e^{-(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)} (\lambda_1/\lambda_2)^{x/2}   I_{|x|}(2\sqrt{\lambda_1 \lambda_2}), \qquad x = \ldots, -1, 0, 1, \ldots$$ \(I_\nu\) modified Bessel function first kind. mean \(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2\) variance \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2\). (\(Y_1\) \(Y_2\) correlated Poisson variables means \(\mu_i\) correlation \(\rho\), difference still Skellam, \(\lambda_i = \mu_i - \rho\sqrt{\mu_1 \mu_2}\).) functions follow conventions stats distribution functions: arguments recycled common length (warning lengths multiples), missing values propagate, invalid rates probabilities give NaN warning, non-integer x density 0 (warning), qskellam returns smallest integer \(x\) \(P(X \le x) \ge p\) (lower.tail = TRUE), qskellam(pskellam(x, ...), ...) recovers x. Numerical methods. dskellam evaluates log Bessel function directly, log = TRUE finite accurate input: besselI reliable, uniform asymptotic expansion large orders, stable downward recurrence large arguments, power series besselI underflows. relative error \(10^{-12}\) rates least \(10^7\), \(10^{-9}\) extremely unequal large rates \((10^6, 10^3)\). pskellam uses non-central chi-square identity Johnson (1959) pchisq \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 \le 10^4\), otherwise, well tails pchisq underflows, sums log-pmf directly toward nearer tail, far tails exact log scale. qskellam starts Cornish-Fisher approximation searches integers pskellam. rskellam returns difference two rpois draws. dskellam.sp pskellam.sp second-order saddlepoint approximation pmf Lugannani-Rice approximation cdf Butler's second continuity correction (Butler 2007). relative error order \(1/(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)^2\) \(1/(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\) respectively; provided users want approximations used dskellam pskellam.

text: cumulant generating function \(X = Y_1 - Y_2\) \(K(t) = \lambda_1(e^t - 1) + \lambda_2(e^{-t} - 1)\), cumulants \(\kappa_r = \lambda_1 + (-1)^r \lambda_2\): mean \(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2\), variance \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2\), skewness \((\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)/(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)^{3/2}\) excess kurtosis \(1/(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)\). Raw moments follow cumulants recursion \(\mu'_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \binom{n-1}{k} \kappa_{n-k} \mu'_k\), central moments recursion \(\kappa_1 = 0\). generating functions \(M(t) = E[e^{tX}] = \exp\{K(t)\}\), \(\varphi(t) = E[e^{itX}] = \exp\{\lambda_1(e^{}-1) + \lambda_2(e^{-}-1)\}\) \(G(z) = E[z^X] = \exp\{\lambda_1(z-1) + \lambda_2(1/z-1)\}\).
